points.title: 早年学徒
points.description: 1471年5月21日，阿尔布雷希特·丢勒出生于神圣罗马帝国纽伦堡的一个金匠家庭。他的父亲阿尔布雷希特·丢勒也是一位金匠，来自匈牙利。从13岁起，丢勒开始在父亲的金匠作坊当学徒，但很快展现出对绘画的浓厚兴趣和能力。1486年，15岁的丢勒成为著名画家米夏埃尔·沃格穆特的学徒，在纽伦堡开始了他的艺术生涯。这段早期经历奠定了他扎实的绘画基础，并培养了他对细节的敏锐观察力。
points.descriptionEn: Born on May 21, 1471, in Nuremberg to a goldsmith family of Hungarian origin, Albrecht Dürer began his artistic journey at age 13 in his father's workshop. In 1486, at 15, he became an apprentice to the renowned painter Michael Wolgemut, where he received comprehensive training in painting, woodcutting, and engraving. This early period in Nuremberg established his technical foundation and developed his keen observational skills that would later define his artistic style.

points.title: 游学历练
points.description: 1490年，完成学徒期后，丢勒开始了为期四年的游学生涯。他穿越了德国南部和瑞士，访问了巴塞尔、斯特拉斯堡和科尔马等地。这段旅程中，他接触了不同地区的艺术风格，学习了意大利文艺复兴的艺术理念，并创作了早期作品如《自画像》(1493年)。1492年，他在巴塞尔为《启示录》木刻版画绘制插图，这标志着他作为版画家的开始。这段游学经历极大地拓宽了他的艺术视野，为他后来的创作奠定了多元化的艺术基础。
points.descriptionEn: After completing his apprenticeship in 1490, Dürer embarked on a four-year journey through southern Germany and Switzerland. He visited cities like Basel, Strasbourg, and Colmar, where he encountered diverse artistic styles and absorbed Italian Renaissance ideas. During this period, he created his early works including the famous Self-Portrait (1493) and began his career as a printmaker by illustrating the Apocalypse woodcuts in Basel (1492). This wandering journey significantly broadened his artistic perspective and laid a diverse foundation for his later work.

points.title: 早期创作
points.description: 1494年，23岁的丢勒回到纽伦堡，并与铜匠女儿阿格内斯·弗雷结婚。同年，他创作了第一幅版画杰作《启示录》系列木刻版画，这使他迅速在欧洲艺术界获得声誉。1495年，他在纽伦堡开设了自己的工作室，专注于版画和油画创作。这一时期，他创作了《大受难》系列、《骑士、死亡与魔鬼》等重要作品，并发展出独特的艺术风格，融合了德国传统与意大利文艺复兴元素。1500年，他创作了著名的自画像，展现出对自我形象的深刻探索和自信的艺术态度。
points.descriptionEn: Returning to Nuremberg in 1494 at age 23, Dürer married Agnes Frey, daughter of a copper engraver. The same year, he created his first major masterpiece, the Apocalypse woodcut series, which quickly established his reputation across Europe. In 1495, he opened his own workshop focusing on printmaking and painting. During this period, he produced significant works like the Great Passion series, Knight, Death, and the Devil, and developed his distinctive style blending German traditions with Italian Renaissance elements. In 1500, he created his famous self-portrait, demonstrating profound self-exploration and confident artistic expression.

points.title: 意大利之旅
points.description: 1505年，丢勒首次前往意大利艺术中心威尼斯，这次旅行对他的艺术风格产生了深远影响。在威尼斯，他受到了威尼斯画派大师乔凡尼·贝利尼的高度赞赏，两人建立了深厚的友谊。丢勒学习了意大利的色彩运用和透视技法，同时将德国的精细线条与意大利的柔和色彩相结合。在威尼斯期间，他创作了《亚当与夏娃》等重要作品，并完成了著名的《祈祷之手》素描。这次意大利之旅使丢勒的艺术达到了新的高度，也使他成为连接北方文艺复兴与意大利文艺复兴的重要桥梁。
points.descriptionEn: In 1505, Dürer made his first journey to Venice, the artistic center of Italy, a trip that profoundly influenced his artistic style. In Venice, he received high praise from Giovanni Bellini, with whom he developed a deep friendship. Dürer studied Italian color application and perspective techniques while combining German precision with Italian softness. During this period, he created important works like Adam and Eve and completed the famous Praying Hands drawing. This Italian journey elevated his art to new heights and established him as a crucial bridge between Northern and Italian Renaissance.

points.title: 艺术巅峰
points.description: 1507年回到纽伦堡后，丢勒进入了艺术创作的巅峰时期。他创作了《默示录》系列、《圣哲罗姆》等代表作，并开始深入研究人体比例和透视理论，撰写了《人体比例四书》等重要理论著作。1514年，他创作了版画杰作《骑士、死亡与魔鬼》和《忧郁I》，展现了他对复杂主题的深刻理解。1518年，他成为纽伦堡城市议会的官方画家，享有崇高地位。晚年，他继续创作了大量肖像画、风景画和版画，同时致力于艺术理论研究。1528年4月6日，丢勒在纽伦堡逝世，享年56岁，被公认为德国文艺复兴时期最伟大的艺术家。
points.descriptionEn: After returning to Nuremberg in 1507, Dürer entered his peak creative period. He produced masterpieces like the Apocalypse series and St. Jerome, and began in-depth research on human proportions and perspective theory, writing important theoretical works including Four Books on Human Proportions. In 1514, he created the iconic engravings Knight, Death, and the Devil and Melencolia I, demonstrating his profound understanding of complex themes. By 1518, he had become the official painter of the Nuremberg city council, enjoying high status. In his later years, he continued creating numerous portraits, landscapes, and prints while dedicating himself to art theory. Dürer died in Nuremberg on April 6, 1528, at age 56, and is widely regarded as the greatest artist of the German Renaissance.

supporter.zh: 丢勒被视为北方文艺复兴的伟大先驱，他将意大利文艺复兴的理想与德国哥特式的传统完美融合。他的版画作品开创了欧洲版画艺术的新纪元，对后世艺术家产生深远影响。作为多才多艺的艺术家，他在绘画、版画、艺术理论等领域均有卓越贡献，被誉为'德国的达芬奇'。丢勒的作品不仅展现了精湛的技艺，更体现了对人文主义的深刻理解和对自然科学的严谨态度，为德国艺术的发展奠定了基础。
supporter.en: Dürer is celebrated as a great pioneer of the Northern Renaissance, perfectly blending Italian Renaissance ideals with German Gothic traditions. His printmaking work revolutionized European print art and profoundly influenced later generations. As a versatile artist, he made outstanding contributions to painting, printmaking, and art theory, earning him the title 'the German Leonardo.' His works not only demonstrate exceptional technical skill but also reflect deep understanding of humanism and scientific rigor, laying the foundation for the development of German art.

critic.zh: 批评者指出丢勒的作品有时过于追求技术完美而缺乏情感深度，特别是在后期作品中。他过于强调理论研究和数学比例，有时使作品显得机械和冷峻。此外，丢勒对意大利艺术的崇拜也受到一些德国本土艺术家的批评，认为他过于迎合意大利标准而忽视了德国本土艺术特色。他的宗教题材作品也被认为缺乏创新，多是对传统主题的重复演绎，而非真正的宗教体验表达。
critic.en: Critics argue that Dürer's works sometimes prioritize technical perfection over emotional depth, particularly in his later pieces. His emphasis on theoretical research and mathematical proportions is seen by some as making his work appear mechanical and cold. Additionally, his admiration for Italian art was criticized by some German artists who believed he catered too much to Italian standards while neglecting indigenous German artistic characteristics. His religious works are also considered lacking innovation, often seen as repetitions of traditional themes rather than expressions of genuine religious experience.

objective.zh: 在历史学界，丢勒被公认为连接北方与南方文艺复兴的关键人物，他的艺术成就超越了国界，影响了整个欧洲艺术发展。在流行文化中，丢勒的形象常与文艺复兴时期的艺术创新和人文精神联系在一起，他的自画像和版画作品成为艺术史上的标志性图像。他的《祈祷之手》和《骑士、死亡与魔鬼》等作品已成为文化符号，被广泛引用和重新诠释。丢勒的艺术遗产不仅体现在他的作品本身，还在于他建立的艺术理论体系和对后世艺术家的影响，使他成为艺术史上不可忽视的重要人物。
objective.en: In historical scholarship, Dürer is recognized as a pivotal figure connecting the Northern and Southern Renaissances, with artistic achievements that transcended national boundaries and influenced European art development. In popular culture, his image is often associated with artistic innovation and humanism of the Renaissance period. His self-portraits and prints like Praying Hands and Knight, Death, and the Devil have become iconic images in art history, widely referenced and reinterpreted. Dürer's artistic legacy extends beyond his works to include his theoretical contributions and influence on later artists, making him an indispensable figure in art history.

self.zh: 艺术存在于自然中，谁能将它从自然中提取出来，谁就是艺术家。
self.en: Art is hidden in nature. He who can extract it from nature, he is an artist.

others.zh: 丢勒是德国艺术的最高典范，他的作品完美地融合了北方严谨的精确性与南方优雅的流畅性。
others.en: Dürer is the highest exemplar of German art, whose works perfectly combine the rigor of the North with the elegance of the South.
